title: Petra and the Oath
premise: Bram Coldharbour, a nonbinary beast-speaker who has hidden their gift since magic was outlawed twelve years ago, discovers the border wards fell the same night the stars went out because someone severed the ancient covenant between the human realms and the wild. Hunted by the usurper's witch-finders and reluctantly allied with Petra Vane, a disgraced ward-keeper who once arrested Bram's mentor, they journey to the Oathstone at the heart of the wild to reforge the covenant. Along the way Bram learns their gift is not a curse but the missing half of the oath itself, and that staying invisible cost them the belonging they always craved. In the climax, Bram speaks with the voice of every beast at once to bind the new covenant, sacrificing their anonymity forever; the stars reignite, the usurper's armies falter, and Bram and Petra choose each other over the duties that once divided them.
about_author: Edmund Pemberton is the pen name of a former field naturalist who spent a decade cataloguing birdsong before turning to fantasy. They write stories about outsiders who discover that the thing that made them strange was the thing that made them necessary.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In the free city of Greyhollow, Bram sells harmless charms by day and whispers to stray cats by night, keeping their beast-speech secret. When every star vanishes at once and the city's border wards collapse with a sound like breaking glass, a dying fox staggers into their shop speaking a single word: 'Oathstone.' The beat is dread cracking open a carefully small life.

chapters.title: Witch-Finders at the Door
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The usurper's witch-finders sweep Greyhollow, and Bram's neighbor is dragged away for a charm gone visibly wrong. Bram flees through the sewers guided by rats, only to be cornered—and saved—by Petra Vane, a former ward-keeper stripped of rank for refusing to falsify reports about the wards' decay. The beat is reluctant alliance born of mutual distrust.

chapters.title: What Petra Buried
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra reveals she helped arrest Bram's mentor, Sela, twelve years ago, and has spent her disgrace trying to learn what really happened to the covenant. She carries Sela's confiscated journal, written in a cipher only a beast-speaker can read. Bram agrees to travel with her—not forgiving her, but needing her. The beat is guilt meeting guarded hope.

chapters.title: The Road of Quiet Beasts
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Outside the cities, the wild is eerily silent: animals flee or have forgotten how to speak as the covenant decays. Bram coaxes speech from a wounded elk who remembers fragments of the old oath, learning that the covenant required two voices—one human, one wild—and that it was broken from the human side. The beat is grief for a world going mute.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Harvest
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The pair witnesses a conscript column burning hedgerows and caging 'speaking beasts,' and learns the usurper, Aldric Vey, severed the covenant deliberately to starve the wild of power and feed it into his own war-magic. Petra recognizes the officer commanding the column: her former protégé. The beat is horror hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Sela's Cipher
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Deciphering Sela's journal in an abandoned waystation, Bram learns Sela is alive—imprisoned in Vey's citadel because she refused to name her successor, the second voice needed to reforge the oath. Worse: the journal hints the successor's gift must be strong enough to speak for all beasts at once. Bram realizes why they were always different. The beat is terror at being chosen.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Refuse
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Seeking aid in the free city of Marrowgate, they find its council willing to negotiate surrender rather than fight without the wards. Petra publicly breaks with the institutions she served, denouncing the council and burning her old commission. A handful of young ward-keepers defect to follow her. The beat is love of duty transformed into duty to something truer.

chapters.title: The Citadel of Ash
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Infiltrating Vey's citadel, Bram finds Sela aged and half-broken, and frees her during a diversion Petra stages among the defectors. Confronting Vey, Bram learns his final secret: he was once a beast-speaker too, cast out and maimed, and broke the covenant so no one would ever hold a gift he lost. The beat is pity entangled with fury.

chapters.title: The Oathstone
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the Oathstone, Vey's armies close in as Sela begins the rite—but her stolen years have thinned her gift past use, and the stone stays dark. Bram steps forward and speaks with the voice of every surviving beast at once, the covenant reforging through them in agony and light while Petra holds the line below. The stars reignite mid-battle. The beat is self-annihilation becoming selfhood.

chapters.title: A Voice That Cannot Hide
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The armies scatter as the wild wakes; Vey, hearing the oath spoken whole, surrenders without a sword drawn. Sela, freed, becomes teacher where she was prisoner, and the free cities must now share power with the speaking wild. Bram, no longer able to pass as ordinary, opens a school for gifted children with Petra beside them—at last belonging, loudly. The beat is quiet joy after sacrifice.
